 Justin Reid Fits the Bills and Jaguars, and the 2-5 Saints Should Take Whatever They Can Get
 Originally posted on
 Athlon Sports 
  | 
 By Neal Coolong
  | 
 Last updated Nov 4, 2026 5:26 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 Justin Reid has a market, even if his tape this season doesn’t make the strongest case for one. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler named the Saints safety as New Orleans’ likeliest trade piece in the network’s deadline preview for all 32 teams , noting that multiple teams need safety help, from Buffalo to Jacksonville.
 Fowler laid out the profile. Reid is 29 with 124 career starts, he’s due $9.3 million this season and his guarantees run out in 2027. For a 2-5 team that just made a coaching change and already had him in its trade rumor mix , that’s a player worth moving now.
 Justin Reid’s 2026 numbers lower the price
 Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
 Reid has been on the field plenty, with 444 snaps, but he has struggled. His 44.4 overall grade ranks 93rd of 98 qualified safeties, according to PFF , and he has allowed 20 catches and a 131.9 passer rating in coverage without an interception or a pass breakup. He also has eight missed tackles.
 That’s why the return should be modest. A buyer would be paying for the safety who started for two Super Bowl winners in Kansas City and has rarely missed time, and betting that a better defense around him brings that player back.
 The Saints won’t save money, and that’s fine
 Reid signed a three-year, $31.5 million deal in 2025, and the Saints converted $7.95 million of his salary into a bonus this year, according to Over the Cap . ESPN’s Katherine Terrell noted that New Orleans won’t gain much cap space from any trade because of those restructures. His 2027 cap hit jumps to $13.14 million, though, and that’s money the Saints shouldn’t want to carry for a 30-year-old coming off this season.
 The fits are real. Buffalo released C.J. Gardner-Johnson this week and is shopping for a safety, and Jacksonville has the playoff standing to add a veteran. A late Day 3 pick, or even a pick swap, gets the Saints out of next year’s number and opens snaps for younger players before Sunday’s game against the Browns. Whatever the offer is, New Orleans should take it.
